halt_handoff.text:
Loop 1 ended at HALT_DRY_RUN — --dry-run was set on this invocation, so I ran Step 0 (Discovery), Step 1 (Critic), and Step 2 (Architect plan) but stopped before Step 3 (Execution). No code changes. No commit.

This run is SCOPED to BenchHypeKit/Sources/BenchHypeSettingsFeature — the scorecard and findings are claims about that subtree, not the repository.

Targeted Priority-1 finding: F1 (stable_id F-025) — Derived display state (enum-to-user-text mapping) lives in feature views at three sites.

The plan I would execute (in CURRENT_REVIEW.md "Loop 1 Plan (dry-run)" section):
  Files to change: BenchHypeKit/Sources/BenchHypeDomain/Values/Route.swift, BenchHypeKit/Sources/BenchHypeApplication/Projections/SettingsViewState.swift, BenchHypeKit/Sources/BenchHypeApplication/State/BackupState.swift, BenchHypeKit/Sources/BenchHypeSettingsFeature/DiagnosticsView.swift, BenchHypeKit/Sources/BenchHypeSettingsFeature/BackupSettingsView.swift, BenchHypeKit/Tests/BenchHypeSettingsFeatureTests/SettingsViewStateTests.swift, BenchHypeKit/Tests/BenchHypeSettingsFeatureTests/DiagnosticsViewSnapshotTests.swift
  Files NOT to touch: AppReducer*.swift, SettingsDraft, IntentDispatcher, DiagnosticsReducer.swift, CuesFileStore.swift, RootScene.swift, PaywallView.swift, HelpView.swift, SettingsScreenContext.swift, UITestIdentifiers.swift, UI test targets
  Blast radius: bounded to the change list above
  Expected scorecard impact: state_management 9.0→9.5; domain_modeling 9.0→9.5; simplicity residual queued→accepted

Note: backlog item 3 (F-026) is blocked on an unconditional AGENTS.md code-vs-doc stop-and-ask (render rule vs RootScene wiring disagree on Apple Music availability); an execution loop reaching it must route to the owner's decision, not guess.

Next step options:
  (a) Execute the plan — re-invoke "/contest-refactor" (no flag). The --dry-run flag is invocation-scoped; absence of the flag means execute. No --reset needed.
  (b) Re-plan with a different target — edit the Improvement Backlog in CURRENT_REVIEW.md to promote a different finding to Priority 1. After reordering items, the next Step-1 emit re-derives priority numbers; no manual renumbering is needed. Then re-invoke "/contest-refactor --dry-run" to see the new plan.
  (c) Abort — leave the dry-run state on disk; nothing was changed.

verdict: Good app, but not top-tier yet
verdict_explanation: Scoped claim (BenchHypeSettingsFeature subtree only): a small, disciplined, reducer-honest feature — 1,843 lines, zero stored adapter state, zero unstructured Tasks, single dispatch path. It is held below the 9.5 bar by view-side derived display state at three sites that the repo's own projection contract already forbids, an untested control-to-intent mapping on the main settings screen, and a composition interface whose permissive defaults and manually-coupled availability fields admit lying UI states.

architecture_quality.residual_blocking_10: Permissive defaults (appleMusicAvailable=false, no-op closure defaults) plus manually-synchronized availability fields on the public composition interface

data_flow.residual_blocking_10: Diagnostic trace gate is a string-keyed UserDefaults channel duplicated at three sites instead of flowing through the typed seam
data_flow.residual_rationale_or_backlog_ref: Forced by the features-no-adapter-imports rule and mechanically enforced: named gate applemusic-trace-key-sync verified live at scripts/check_boundaries.sh:1195-1208 and green this loop (boundaries: ok, 108 rules); moving the key through state would add launch-path cost to a default-off diagnostic switch

concurrency.proof: G25 walk: zero CheckedContinuation/withCheckedThrowingContinuation occurrences in scope (grep-listed this loop), no delegate audit applicable; zero unstructured Task (README claim verified); .task lifecycle-scoped (DiagnosticsView.swift:42-45); @MainActor value-type context; re-entry guarded at the reducer seam (DiagnosticsReducer.swift:15)

credibility.proof: Doc-vs-code sweep of scope: README rule claims true; trace-key comment's gate claim verified real (check_boundaries.sh:1195-1208); AppBuildInfo comments match code; ADR-0003-consistency of transition copy verified against CONTEXT.md vocabulary

findings.title: Derived display state (enum-to-user-text mapping) lives in feature views at three sites
findings.why_it_matters: The repo's own Hard Rule 5 and its in-source projection contract put derived display state in *ViewState projections and on the enum type (Hard Rule 4); three view-side switches violate that pattern in the reviewed subtree, and the class was already swept and fixed elsewhere twice (registry F-001, F-008/F-009).
findings.what_is_wrong: DiagnosticsView resolves domain enum OutputDestination and application enum InterruptionState to user-facing labels; BackupSettingsView resolves BackupPhase to status copy. Product messaging is shaped at the read-site instead of the owner-site.
evidence: BenchHypeKit/Sources/BenchHypeDomain/Values/Route.swift:22-41 (enum home; isWireless on type, display label is the only interpretation outside it)
BenchHypeKit/Sources/BenchHypeApplication/Projections/AppSnapshot.swift:210-212 (in-repo precedent: projection owns the display string)
findings.leverage_impact: A new surface reporting backup/interruption/route status must re-derive the strings; only views can answer them today.
findings.locality_impact: Status-copy edits touch feature files now and owner files later, drifting.
findings.metric_signal: scanner control-queue candidate statusMessage (decision_count 5 / 11 lines) — corroborating, not deciding
findings.why_weakens_submission: Violates the subtree's own documented single-owner display rule at three sites; contained (no live drift demonstrated), so Noticeable — but the pattern across one module reduces ownership credibility.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Byte-identical relocation: displayName computed on OutputDestination (its home, BenchHypeDomain/Values/Route.swift — Hard Rule 4's canonical form); interruption display field on DiagnosticsViewState (its home projection, Projections/SettingsViewState.swift); statusMessage computed on BackupState.phase's owning type (State/BackupState.swift). Delete the three view functions; relocate string assertions into SettingsViewStateTests through the projection interface. No new seam or protocol.

findings.title: Context composition admits lying states: permissive defaults plus manually-synchronized availability fields
findings.why_it_matters: Hard Rule 3's parallel-fields signal: appleMusicAvailable and state.appleMusicEntitlement must agree, nothing in the type enforces it, and the defaults (=false, ={} closures) convert a forgotten wire-up into a silently-wrong UI instead of a compile error.
findings.what_is_wrong: The render rule claims 'available && entitlement nil -> Authorize (cold-start)' is a reachable state, while the only production construction derives availability from entitlement non-nilness, making that branch unreachable. Code and doc disagree on the invariant — per AGENTS.md the doc is treated as binding and the conflict is reported here; the conflict blocks autonomous fix.
findings.leverage_impact: Every future call site must re-learn the coupling rule to wire the struct honestly.
findings.locality_impact: The availability fact is owned jointly by caller, context, and view branching.
findings.why_weakens_submission: A public composition interface whose lying states are reachable and whose doc and wiring disagree about which states exist is a credibility and state-ownership weakness; latent, not live — Noticeable.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Blocked pending owner adjudication of the doc-vs-code conflict (AGENTS.md stop-and-ask, not coverable by the Hard Rule 3/4 safe harbor): if the render rule is the invariant, RootScene.swift:341 is the wrong derivation and the model needs a build-time availability signal; if the derivation is the invariant, the doc branch is stale. Then replace bool + two closures + defaults with one sum type (enum AppleMusicAccess { case unavailable; case available(authorize:, refresh:) }) and drop the defaults; two construction sites update.

findings.title: DiagnosticsView is public with zero cross-module consumers
findings.why_it_matters: Repeat of the api-surface-scope class retired twice in this repo's registry (F-022, F-024): unjustified public widens the module's supported surface for no caller.
findings.what_is_wrong: Only same-module consumers exist (the in-file NavigationLink in SettingsScreenContent and @testable snapshot tests); no app-target call site survives this loop's repo-wide grep.
evidence: BenchHypeKit/Tests/BenchHypeSettingsFeatureTests/DiagnosticsViewSnapshotTests.swift:3 (@testable import — internal is sufficient; precedent PaywallView demoted at af18aebc with snapshot tests green)
HelpView public is justified by BenchHype/BenchHype/BenchHypeApp.swift:92 (contrast: a real cross-module consumer exists there, not here)
findings.leverage_impact: None gained; the public initializer exposes cross-module reach no module uses.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Cosmetic in isolation; a third instance of a class the repo already invested in cleaning is a pattern signal on API-surface discipline.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Drop public from DiagnosticsView and its init; compile matrix is the oracle (same mechanics as af18aebc). Fold into F1's loop (same file, one line).

findings.title: The settings control-to-intent mapping has no test at any surface
findings.why_it_matters: Sixteen controls bind by keyPath; a mis-wire passes every current gate, and the screen's own playback identifiers were built for tests that do not exist.
findings.what_is_wrong: No SettingsScreenContent render test in the feature target; no UI test consumes settings.playback.* or the tap-action pickers; reducer tests assert intent semantics but cannot see which control dispatches which keyPath. Mutation check: swapping defaultFadeInSeconds/defaultFadeOutSeconds bindings leaves the full pinned suite green.
evidence: BenchHypeKit/Sources/BenchHypeSharedUI/UITestIdentifiers.swift:73,93 (identifiers with zero test consumers — grep across BenchHypeKit/Tests, BenchHypeUITests, BenchHypeMacUITests this loop)
BenchHype/BenchHypeUITests/PaywallUITests.swift:10-48 (contrast: paywall flow does have a UI test)
findings.leverage_impact: None today — the existing snapshot mechanics can pin the mapping without new machinery.
findings.locality_impact: The flow's tests would not survive a view refactor, the test-shape signal.
findings.why_weakens_submission: An untested mapping on a user-facing settings surface with realistic silent-regression risk caps regression resistance; off the primary playback flow, so Noticeable, not disqualifier.
findings.minimal_correction_path: One value-differentiated render test for SettingsScreenContent using the existing @testable snapshot pattern: distinct fade-in/out and gain values in the fed SettingsViewState make a keyPath swap change the rendered .dump (fadeSlider prints value text, SettingsScreenContent.swift:352-363). No new harness, no new seam.

simplification_check.structurally_necessary: F1 consolidates three enum->display mappings onto their owner types — passes Replace-don't-layer (view helpers deleted, assertions land at the projection interface); F2 removes representable contradiction via a sum type (Hard Rule 3's prescribed shape) once the owner adjudicates the doc conflict.
simplification_check.helpful_simplification: F3 public drop is a one-line deletion riding F1's file pass; the settings flow already lives at the IntentDispatcher seam — the fixes relocate and model, never add layers.
simplification_check.should_not_be_done: A SettingsBinder protocol to make bindings injectable (fails Unified Seam Policy: one adapter, no behavior-faithful fakes); routing the trace-gate key through reducer state (ceremony for a default-off diagnostic already gate-checked against drift).
simplification_check.tests_after_fix: SettingsViewStateTests gains the relocated string assertions (projection interface); new SettingsScreenContentSnapshotTests pins control->value mapping; DiagnosticsViewSnapshotTests unchanged unless serialization moves; no old tests deleted — none mirror the removed helpers.

backlog.title: Move the three view-side enum->display mappings to their owner types; fold the F-027 public drop into the same pass
backlog.why_it_matters: Restores the repo's own single-owner display rule across the subtree and closes a class already retired elsewhere twice.

backlog.title: Add the value-differentiated SettingsScreenContent render test pinning control->value mapping
backlog.why_it_matters: Today the settings-edit flow has no test that fails when a control binds the wrong field.

backlog.title: Collapse appleMusicAvailable + two closure params + defaults into one sum type
backlog.why_it_matters: Removes the representable lying-composition state. Blocked on an unconditional AGENTS.md code-vs-doc stop-and-ask (render rule +AppleMusic.swift:12-24 vs RootScene.swift:341): the owner must adjudicate which side is the invariant before any loop attempts it.

deepening_candidates.source_friction_proven: RootScene.swift:341 manually derives one public parameter from a different projection field to keep the F-026 pair consistent (see Finding F2)
deepening_candidates.why_shallow_or_misplaced: The caller must know the coupling rule; the type cannot. The interface carries three related fields where one state should live.
deepening_candidates.behavior_to_move_behind_interface: Availability branching collapses to one sum-type match at the render site (already partially structured at SettingsScreenContent+AppleMusic.swift:43-69).
deepening_candidates.test_surface_after_change: Same snapshot surfaces; construction becomes exhaustive over two states.
deepening_candidates.smallest_first_step: Owner adjudication of the F-026 invariant (backlog item 3), then the enum.
deepening_candidates.what_not_to_do: Do not inject a protocol or view-model layer; the struct is the right shape, just modeled as a product.

builder_notes.pattern: A repo that documents its display-ownership rule at one enforcement site (AppSnapshot.swift:211 'view stays render-only') still leaks where no grep reaches: view-side switches returning user-facing strings.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: private func ... -> String? whose body is a switch over an enum from another module.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: If a view computes a sentence, a type or a projection computes it instead.
builder_notes.stack_example: DiagnosticsView.swift:81-97 resolves OutputDestination/InterruptionState to labels inside the view while Route.swift:30 keeps isWireless on the type — the label is the orphaned half.

builder_notes.pattern: Permissive defaults on a composition type convert a forgotten wire-up into wrong output instead of a compile error.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: = false / = {} parameters that select user-visible branches.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Defaults only where every defaulted value is safe in every combination; otherwise make the state a sum type.
builder_notes.stack_example: SettingsScreenContext.swift:13-17 — an app that forgets appleMusicAvailable: true renders 'This build was not compiled with Apple Music support' in a build that was.

builder_notes.pattern: Compliance is not clearance — and claims are not checks: a comment asserting its own duplication is 'gate-checked' must be opened before it is filed or accepted.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Prose citing an enforcement mechanism (a script, a test, a rule) as the safety net for a structural shortcut.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: grep for the named check before trusting or filing the claim.
builder_notes.stack_example: AppleMusicPlaylistTracksView.swift:8-12 claimed the three-way key literal is gate-synced; check_boundaries.sh:1195-1208 shows a real named check (applemusic-trace-key-sync) — finding converted to accepted residual.

builder_notes.pattern: Priority-1 accounting: P1 (F-025) moves state_management and domain_modeling 9.0->9.5. The further-from-target candidate F-028 (test_strategy 8.5) was considered first under distance-to-target and ranks second on expected marginal gain — two dimensions onto the target line versus one halfway, at equal severity; neither fails the SPT, so gain decides. F-026 ties on state-ownership merit but is blocked by the code-vs-doc stop-and-ask (criterion 0: ranked on merit, blocker named, next actionable item taken). Stalled-Dimension Sweep: N/A at loop 1 (floor loop 4). Adversarial Pass on Accepted Residuals: N/A at loop 1 (no prior accepted residual in this run).
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: A ranking driven purely by 'which finding looks worst' ratchets the nearest-target dimension while the rest stand still.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Rank by expected marginal contest gain, name the accounting sentence every loop.

builder_notes.pattern: Scorecard humility check — three least-confident claims: (1) state_management 9.0 vs 9.5: the F1 trio is 28 lines with no live drift; a reviewer could meet the 9-anchor and accept it — scored unmet because the anchor is owner-site separation itself (DiagnosticsView.swift:81). (2) F2 'Split and ambiguous': if availability is by definition build-time, RootScene.swift:341 is the single source and only the doc is stale — both readings fit current source. (3) concurrency 10: the zero-continuation claim covers this subtree only; the .task refresh pair leans on the out-of-scope reducer guard (DiagnosticsReducer.swift:15), quoted, not re-derived.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Any ceiling resting on a mechanism outside the reviewed scope.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Cite the boundary of what was actually walked, per dimension.
builder_notes.stack_example: Scoped-run Discovery sentence: all claims are subtree claims, not repository claims.

narrative: Place — scoped to BenchHypeSettingsFeature: a disciplined feature surface (single dispatch path, honest seams, verified doc claims, ADR-consistent copy, clean concurrency) held below winning structure by one repeated ownership pattern (display shaping in views, F-025), an untested control-mapping surface (F-028), and a composition interface with lying-state defaults (F-026, blocked on an owner call the repo itself mandates as unconditional). Simplification helped — the strongest fixes are relocations and a deletion, adding no seam. Runtime ownership is trustworthy where enforced; concurrency is trustworthy and clean; tests under-protect the main screen. Future work risk is a SettingsBinder protocol — the fake-clean reward to refuse.
